Article Title: Govt condemns vandalism of Indian embassy in Slovenia
Article Text:
Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected.

NEW DELHI: Condemning the defacement of Indian embassy premises in Slovenia by Khalistan separatists, the govt urged law enforcement authorities elsewhere too to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups.Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected."We have taken up the matter strongly with Slovenian authorities, both in New Delhi and in Ljubljana so that the perpetrators behind such reprehensible acts are held accountable to the full extent of the law," it said."We also call upon law enforcement authorities elsewhere to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups," it added.In recent years, Indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-Khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries, including Australia, Canada, UK and the US.
Article Summary: Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the vienna convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected. In recent years, indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries, including australia, canada, uk and us.

Article Title: India move will muddle border talks: China
Article Text:
State-run Global Times quoted Chinese experts as saying India’s move would not alter the legal status of the disputed territory but could complicate future boundary negotiations.

GUWAHATI: China has hit back sharply at India for assigning standard names to 27 geographical locations in Arunachal Pradesh, with the state-run Global Times claiming these areas are in China's 'Zangnan' region - Beijing's term for Arunachal Pradesh and adjoining areas that it claims as part of Tibet Autonomous part.The daily reiterated that Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a routine press briefing on April 14 that the Zangnan region is China's territory and "China does not recognise the so-called 'Arunachal Pradesh' illegally set up by India. It is fully within China's sovereign rights for the Chinese govt to issue standard names for some of the places in Zangnan."The reaction came three days after India's Survey of India updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument in Arunachal Pradesh, which govt said was an exercise to ensure the "correct identification" of places and enhance public awareness of their geographical and historical significance.Global Times reported on Sunday night that the mapping by India came shortly after the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on China-India Border Affairs (WMCC), held on Aug 6 in New Delhi, where officials from both sides discussed issues including boundary delimitation, border management and control, mechanism building and cross-border cooperation."India's latest move is essentially an attempt to reinforce its claims over disputed territory and counter China's sovereignty position," Guo Xuetang, a professor at Shanghai International Studies University, said.The latest "war of names" adds another layer to an already complex border dispute, even as both sides seek to keep military and diplomatic channels open.
Article Summary: State-run global times quoted chinese experts as saying india’s move would not alter the legal status of the disputed territory but could complicate future boundary negotiations. India's survey of india updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument.

Article Title: Air India turbulence scare: Airbus and French agency to join probe into Phuket flight
Article Text:
The aircraft plunged 300ft, injuring many on board

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: European aerospace major Airbus and France's Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety will join the probe to establish what caused the Air India A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi with 145 aboard to suddenly lose altitude by about 300ft last week, injuring many on board.Led by India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), the investigation is examining the twin aspects of the aircraft's mechanical issues and pilot behaviour. Everyone TOI spoke to said what happened mid-flight was indeed "a close shave". Luckily, the aircraft (AI 2379) landed safely at its destination, but 17 people had to be hospitalised.The captain's psychoactive substance screening test was not negative, and the confirmatory test result is not yet officially known. His behaviour on board is under the scanner. "One of the pilots fell in the cockpit and had to be assisted by cabin crew to get back on his seat," said a source. The flight data recorder will reveal mechanical failures, if any, and the cockpit voice recorder will reveal what transpired on the flight deck."Airbus is sending its team to India, and they will reach by Wednesday to inspect the aircraft and work with Air India and AAIB.Being a serious incident, the investigator of the original equipment manufacturer's country (France in this case) is also coming," said a source. An Airbus official said it is "providing technical assistance to the investigating authorities. We are actively supporting the airline and will provide further information as it becomes available".Industry executives said the A320 (VT-EXO) may have suffered a triple hydraulic failure for a few seconds, which is rare. This system uses a fluid under pressure to drive machinery or move mechanical components to power critical elements like wheel brakes, nose wheel steering, landing gear retraction/extension and flight control surfaces. It is also learnt the autopilot became disengaged during that tumultuous time for a few seconds, and the aircraft even got a stall warning.A pilot then steadied the aircraft by pushing the nose down.AI said it can't "comment on any findings or observations related to the investigation" as it "is being conducted by AAIB" and that the airline "will continue to extend our full cooperation to authorities as required". The flight data recorder will reveal the timestamps of the sequence of events - whether the alleged transient hydraulic failure occurred because of the aircraft's rapid descent or whether the aircraft first entered an air pocket and subsequent turbulence caused hydraulic failure.
Article Summary: European aerospace major airbus and france's bureau of enquiry and analysis for civil aviation safety will join the probe. The air india a320 flying from phuket to delhi with 145 aboard suddenly lost altitude by about 300ft last week. 17 people had to be hospitalised. The captain's psychoactive substance screening test was not negative.

Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan begins four-day Mauritius visit

NEW DELHI: Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan on Monday went to Mauritius on a four-day official visit to strengthen bilateral maritime cooperation.The visit is part of India's continued engagement to defence ties with Mauritius, an extremely valued partner in the Indian Ocean Region.During the visit, the Navy chief will interact with the senior leadership of the govt of Mauritius and hold discussions on matters of mutual interest such as maritime security, defence cooperation, capacity building and military collaboration, the Navy said in a statement.Such engagements are aimed at strengthening Indo-Mauritius cooperation in the maritime domain, enhancing operational-level linkages and consolidating the robust strategic partnership between India and Mauritius, it said.The visit of Admiral Swaminathan to Mauritius after assuming charge as the Navy chief underscores the priority India accords to the friendship it shares with Mauritius, anchored in mutual respect, trust and a shared commitment to maritime security, regional cooperation and stability in the Indian Ocean Region.India and Mauritius share a close and enduring maritime partnership.Indian Navy engages regularly with the National Coast Guard through training exchanges, operational interactions including joint exclusive economic zone surveillance, port visits and hydrographic surveys.Both countries also participate and engage with each other in multilateral forums and cooperative initiatives.Mauritius has been a regular participant in key Indian Navy initiatives such as Indian Ocean Naval Symposium, MILAN, International Fleet Review, Goa Maritime Conclave, IOS SAGAR and Exercise AIKEYME, aptly reflecting the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) they share.

Article Title: India adds 11 ports to e-visa scheme; total entry points rises to 88
Article Text:
Total number of airports, seaports and land ports allowing entry of e-visa holders rises to 88

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The government has notified 11 more international ports in the country, including 9 land ports and 2 airports, for the entry of eligible foreigners arriving on electronic visas (e-visas). They can now land with e-visa at Bhopal and Tirupati airports and clear immigration.The additional landports via which e-visa holding foreign nationals can enter India include Attari in Punjab; Gede, Ghojanga and Jaigaon in West Bengal; Darranga in Assam; Agartala in Tripura; Moreh in Manipur; and Haridaspur in Odisha.E-visas currently make up 78% of the total visas issued in the country. India provides approximately 95% e-visas applications in less than 72 hours.The home ministry, in a statement on Monday, said the addition of 11 international ports further enhances attractiveness and utility of electronic visa.The Narendra Modi govt has taken a number of significant initiatives over the last few years to liberalize, streamline and simplify visa regime with a view to facilitating the legitimate foreign travelers while simultaneously ramping up the technological infrastructure to enhance internal security.With the latest addition of 11 international airports to the e-visa scheme, the total number of international ports enabling entry of e-visa holder foreigners has risen to 88, including 37 airports, 38 seaports and 13 land ports.E-visa facility, with electronic travel authorisation (ETA), was introduced in 2014 to liberalize and simplify the Indian visa regime, especially the tourist visa regime. Having taken off with 43 eligible countries, the facility is now available to nationals of 172 countries.E-visa is presently issued under 17 sub-categories; namely tourist visa, mountaineering visa, business visa (six types), medical visa (four types), student visa (two types), transit visa, miscellaneous visa and group visitor visa (cruise).
Article Summary: Total number of airports, seaports and land ports allowing entry of e-visa holders rises to 88. E-visas currently make up 78% of the total visas issued in the country. India provides approximately 95% e-visas applications in less than 72 hours.

Article Title: 'Let voice of people be heard': Speaker Om Birla's emotional appeal to oppn amid Lok Sabha logjam
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Monday made an emotional appeal to floor leaders of all parties to end the logjam in the Lower House and allow Parliament to function without disruptions.During a meeting of the Business Advisory Committee, Birla urged floor leaders to "let the voice of the people be heard", news agency ANI reported, citing sources.The Lok Sabha speaker said key bills should be discussed in the House and there should be no disruption so that members can express their views on legislation being passed by Parliament, sources added."Emphasising the importance of constructive deliberations, meaningful participation and adherence to the highest parliamentary traditions, the Speaker appealed to all parties to extend their cooperation in ensuring the smooth and orderly conduct of the proceedings so that issues concerning the people can be discussed in a comprehensive and productive manner," sources said.The appeal comes amid continued disruptions by the Opposition during the Monsoon Session. Opposition parties have been demanding a response from home minister Amit Shah over alleged police brutality against students protesting the NEET paper leak across the country, as well as a debate on alleged embezzlement of donations from the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.For the 16th consecutive day, the Lower House failed to complete Question Hour due to persistent sloganeering by Opposition members.As many as nine bills have been passed by the Lok Sabha during the ongoing session, but only two have been debated.Earlier in the day, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government was ready for a debate in the Lok Sabha on the student protests and police action. He said the home minister would reply to the debate, but the Opposition should assure the government that it would "not run away" from the debate and listen peacefully.Despite the government's assurance, the bill to establish a National Tribunal Commission was passed by the House without a debate as the Opposition continued its noisy protests.
Article Summary: Lok sabha speaker om birla made an emotional appeal to floor leaders of all parties. He urged floor leaders to "let the voice of the people be heard" the appeal comes amid continued disruptions by the opposition during the monsoon session.

Article Title: 'US has similar laws': Indian envoy Vinay Kwatra clarifies FCRA Bill, shares 'myth vs reality' check
Article Text:
Kwatra issued a “Myth vs. Reality check” on the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill.

‘FCRA does not target any religion’

‘Foreign money inflows have been rising’

‘US has FARA, FATCA’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's Ambassador to the US Vinay Mohan Kwatra on Monday defended the proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), saying the changes are aimed at improving transparency, governance and oversight of foreign funds.In a series of posts on X on Monday, Kwatra issued a “Myth vs. Reality check” on the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026, amid concerns raised by sections of civil society and a US lawmaker over the legislation.Kwatra said regulating foreign financial flows in public and political spaces was a sovereign measure driven by national security concerns and was common in several democracies.“Truth: Regulation of foreign financial flows in public and political spaces is a sovereign step driven by national security concerns. It is an accepted feature of modern governance in many democracies around the world,” he said.Responding to the claim that India was framing a new law to cut off foreign aid to civil society, Kwatra said the proposed legislation did not prohibit Indians from receiving foreign donations or seek to shut down law-abiding organisations.“The fact is that the law does not forbid Indians from receiving foreign donations or shut down law abiding civil society.Tens of thousands of associations are registered under FCRA and routinely receive foreign funds for health, education, disaster relief, research and humanitarian work,” he said.Kwatra said the FCRA was first enacted in India in 1976 and replaced by a new framework in 2010. It was subsequently strengthened through amendments in 2016, 2018 and 2020.“The 2026 Bill and Rules are the next step in the same direction: more transparency, better governance, clearer rules,” he said.Kwatra also rejected allegations that the FCRA amendments "specifically target a particular religion or community."“Truth: Nothing could be farther from it. The Act applies uniformly to all organisations regardless of religion, community or ideology,” he said.He added that faith-based welfare activities, including religious education, maintenance of places of worship and charitable work by organisations of all faiths, would continue to be eligible for foreign funding.Kwatra also rejected claims that the FCRA had adversely affected NGOs and charitable organisations or that the proposed amendments would further restrict their operations.“Truth: In reality, foreign money inflows into India have been rising, not falling. Foreign contributions to registered organisations grew from roughly $1.2 billion in 2010–11 to $2.67 billion in 2024–25,” he said.He said India has more than 3 million NGOs, while only 14,450 have FCRA registration, arguing that the overwhelming majority of civil society organisations fall outside the ambit of the Act.“FCRA does not stop anyone from accepting foreign charity, research grants or humanitarian aid. It asks three things — register, receive the money through laid down process, report what you did with it,” Kwatra said.Addressing concerns that the proposed law would allow the government to seize assets of NGOs, religious charities, places of worship, hospitals and schools dependent on foreign donations, Kwatra said the provision regarding assets was not new.“When a registration is cancelled or surrendered, foreign contributions and the assets created from them already vest in a State Government authority. This has been in force since 2010. It is not new,” he said.According to Kwatra, the 2026 Bill proposes to create a designated authority to safeguard such assets and also provides a mechanism for their return if an organisation restores its FCRA registration.“What the 2026 Bill adds is a designated authority to safeguard those assets — and a way back. If the organisation restores its registration, all assets and unused funds are returned in full,” he said.He also said the proposed legislation contains specific provisions for places of worship.“Places of worship carry their own protection. Where a cancelled association has created property connected to a place of worship, that property goes to another FCRA-registered association of the same faith to ensure continuity of worship,” Kwatra said.Kwatra also dismissed the argument that India was an outlier in regulating foreign funding, pointing to similar laws in other countries.“Truth: The US has had FARA since 1938 and FATCA since 2010. Australia legislated in 2018, Canada in 2024. The UK's scheme came into force in July 2025. The EU is legislating now,” he posted on X.His comments came days after a US lawmaker raised concerns over the proposed FCRA amendments, claiming that the legislation could allow the Indian government to take control of churches and charities.The FCRA Bill, 2026 proposes to empower the government to create a “Designated Authority” to take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such contributions when an organisation's FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or ceases because it is not renewed.The Bill also states that where such assets constitute a place of worship, the Designated Authority must ensure that its religious character is maintained.
Article Summary: Kwatra issued a “myth vs. Reality check” on the proposed fcra amendment bill. ‘fcra does not target any religion’ ‘foreign money inflows into india have been rising, not falling’ the fcra bill, 2026 proposes to empower the government to take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such contributions.

Article Title: Indian envoy meets Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman days after Sheikh Hasina's address in Delhi
Article Text:
After Hasina’s Delhi address, Indian envoy meets Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman

Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi on Monday met Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in a significant diplomatic engagement between the two neighbours.The meeting came a day after Trivedi held a one-on-one discussion with Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman on Sunday, who also attended Monday’s meeting.Speaking to reporters in Dhaka on Sunday after inaugurating a children's corner at the Indian Visa Application Centre, Trivedi expressed optimism about his upcoming meeting with Tarique Rahman and emphasised the importance of direct engagement between the leaders of the two countries."I feel that when... when two leaders meet, a lot of problems are solved. Problems are sorted out when we talk to each other. And I have full confidence that people are together, and the solution will definitely happen... it will happen. I am very confident. There is nothing negative here; everything is positive," Trivedi said."The Prime Minister of Bangladesh... we all respect him a lot. I have listened to his speeches many times, and he talks from his heart.This, I have seen. He is a people's person. And our Prime Minister is also of the people," Trivedi added.The latest diplomatic engagement follows a virtual press interaction by former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in New Delhi on August 5, marking the second anniversary of her ouster in a student-led uprising in 2024. The event drew strong objections from Dhaka.Hasina fled Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, and took refuge in India following the political upheaval that ended her long tenure as prime minister.India has distanced itself from Hasina’s engagement, saying the government has no involvement in the event held in the national capital. Addressing a media briefing on Tuesday, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the event was organised by a "private media entity" and that New Delhi does not endorse any views expressed there."The interaction you refer to is being organised by a private media entity. The government has no involvement whatsoever in it. Neither does it endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum," Jaiswal said.The meeting also comes ahead of India’s invitation to Rahman to attend the BRICS Summit in September in his capacity as the current chair of BIMSTEC.
Article Summary: After hasina’s delhi address, indian envoy meets bangladesh pm tarique rahman. The meeting came a day after trivedi held a one-on-one discussion with bangladesh foreign minister khalilur rahman on sunday. The latest diplomatic engagement follows a virtual press interaction by former pm sheikh hasina in new delhi on august 5.

Article Title: To bypass Bosphorus & Hormuz, Russia moots direct rail link to India
Article Text:
Apart from logistical difficulty and cost, for any option to extend the rail link to India, New Delhi would have to deal with the fact that it would pass through Pakistan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Russian deputy PM Marat Khusnullin has suggested exploring a direct rail link from Moscow to the ‘Indian Ocean’ to avert risks associated with the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz, amid ongoing conflicts, including in West Asia, that have stalled the ambitious India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor. Bosphorus is a narrow, natural strait in Turkey that connects Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.“A rail link to the Indian Ocean should also be explored. Risks related to the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz might require alternative routes: through Turkmenistan, Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan. Any options providing access to India are acceptable,” he told Russian news agency TASS.Experts said constructing a rail link spanning two continents and four countries would be a gigantic challenge. Apart from logistical difficulty and cost, for any option to extend the rail link to India, New Delhi would have to deal with the fact that it would pass through Pakistan, and a lot would depend on obtaining an iron-clad guarantee for securing cooperation and commitment of the hostile neighbour to protect the railway and cargo.The statement does not provide a detailed construction plan, cost estimate or timeline. However, if such a corridor is eventually developed, it could create a direct overland rail freight route linking Russia with India while offering an alternative to traditional maritime shipping routes.Among railway corridors linking multiple nations, Yiwu-Madrid is the longest freight train line in the world — spanning a little over 13,000 km, it connects China’s Yiwu to Spain’s Madrid, traversing eight countries.
Article Summary: Russian deputy pm marat khusnullin has suggested exploring a direct rail link from moscow to the ‘indian ocean’ risks related to the bosphorus and the strait of hormuz might require alternative routes: through turkmenistan, iran, afghanistan, and pakistan.

Article Title: Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei fills 6 top military posts amid wartime leadership overhaul
Article Text:
The appointments come as Iran seeks to reinforce its military command structure following the deaths and displacement of senior commanders during the conflict.

Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei has appointed six senior commanders to key positions in the country’s military establishment, filling top posts in the armed forces, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), IRGC Navy and Basij.Major General Ali Abdollahi has been named Chief of Staff of Iran’s Armed Forces, with Brigadier General Kioumars Heydari appointed as his deputy, according to a series of decrees issued by Khamenei.The IRGC will also get a new commander. Brigadier general Ahmad Vahidi has been promoted to the rank of Major General and appointed as the force’s Commander-in-Chief. Major General Mostafa Izadi will serve as his deputy.The reshuffle also changes the leadership of two key IRGC-linked organisations. Rear Admiral Ali Azmaei has been appointed to head the IRGC Navy, while Hojjatoleslam Walmuslimin Hossein Taeb will lead the Basij Resistance Force.Iran’s Supreme Leader’s office said the appointments were made through separate decrees setting out the new responsibilities of the commanders.The statement said, "Based on these decrees, Major General Ali Abdollahi, a pilot of the Revolutionary Guards, was appointed as the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces, and Brigadier General Kioumars Heydari was appointed as the Deputy Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces."On the IRGC leadership, it said, "Also, Brigadier General Ahmad Vahidi was given the rank of Major General and became the Commander-in-Chief of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, and Major General Mostafa Izadi assumed the responsibility of succeeding the Commander-in-Chief of the Corps."The statement added, "Following these decrees, the responsibility of commanding the IRGC Navy was assigned to Rear Admiral Ali Azmaei, and the leadership of the Basij Mostazafan Organisation was assigned to Hojjatoleslam Walmuslimin Hossein Taeb."The appointments are the latest in a series of senior security and military changes announced by Mojtaba Khamenei On Sunday, he appointed former IRGC commander Mohsen Rezaee as his representative to Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, replacing Mohammad Baqir Zolghadr.In the decree, an account attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei said, "Dr Mohsen Rezaee, considering your valuable experience, I am hereby appointing you, who were one of the first commanders in the triumphant 8-Year Sacred Defence, to be my representative in the Supreme National Security Council."The post was previously held by Ali Larijani, who was assassinated in US-Israeli strikes in March.The latest appointments also come as President Masoud Pezeshkian sought to dismiss concerns over Khamenei’s health. Pezeshkian said the Supreme Leader was "completely healthy" after what he described as a "very good meeting" with him, ISNA reported on Monday.
Article Summary: Iran’s supreme leader ayatollah mojtaba hosseini khamenei has appointed six senior commanders to key positions. The appointments come as iran seeks to reinforce its military command structure following the deaths and displacement of senior commanders during the conflict.

Article Title: Watch: Chinese rocket explodes shortly after liftoff from Wenchang spaceport
Article Text: A Chinese Long March 7A rocket carrying the ChinaSat-4B satellite exploded shortly after liftoff from the Wenchang Space Launch Site in southern China on Monday, news agency Reuters reported.According to footage circulating on social media, the rocket exploded near the coastal spaceport about 85 seconds after liftoff.The rocket lifted off at 8.02 pm Beijing time but encountered a flight anomaly shortly after launch, leading to the failure of the mission, according to state news agency Xinhua.The report said the cause of the anomaly was being further analysed.The incident marks the first known failure of the Long March 7A since its maiden flight in March 2020. The rocket returned to service in 2021 and has since completed a series of successful missions.China National Radio initially reported the launch, but the report was later made unavailable. China's space authorities have not yet issued an official statement on the mission's outcome.According to SpaceNews, the Long March 7A is designed to carry satellites into geosynchronous orbit and has increasingly been used as a replacement for the older, hypergolic Long March 3B for such missions.The Long March 7A made its debut in March 2020, with its maiden flight also ending in failure. It subsequently completed several successful launches, including the Tianlian-3 (01) satellite mission in late July.
Article Summary: A chinese long march 7a rocket carrying the chinasat-4b satellite exploded shortly after liftoff from the wenchang space launch site in southern china. The rocket encountered a flight anomaly shortly after launch, leading to the failure of the mission. It is the first known failure since its maiden flight in march 2020.

Article Title: 'Need conducive environment': Bangladesh PM on India ties as Hasina eyes return to Dhaka
Article Text:
Bangladesh PM Tariq Rehman has called for a "conducive environment" to improve ties with India.

ALSO READ |

What Hasina said

Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for a "conducive environment" to improve ties with India, as Dhaka continues to seek New Delhi's cooperation on the extradition of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina.Rahman made the remarks on Monday during his first meeting with India's new high commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi.His comments come as his six-month-old government seeks to stabilise relations with Bangladesh's largest neighbour while addressing several contentious issues that emerged after Hasina was removed from power in August 2024.The Prime Minister's Office said Rahman "emphasised the need to create a conducive environment to further advance the bilateral relations between the two countries".Dhaka also called on New Delhi to expedite Hasina's extradition, according to the statement.Hasina has been living in India since the fall of her government. She faces legal proceedings in Bangladesh and was sentenced to death in November.The extradition issue has gained fresh prominence following Hasina's recent public appearance. She addressed an online audio conference, her first interaction with the media since leaving Bangladesh, and said she would return to the country in December.The remarks renewed attention on her continued presence and political activities in India and prompted a strong reaction from Dhaka.Bangladesh's foreign ministry criticised India for allowing Hasina to address the event, saying the decision was deeply hurtful and that Bangladesh was outraged.India has said it is examining Dhaka's extradition request in accordance with its legal and judicial procedures.The meeting with Trivedi came as both sides sought to signal a willingness to keep diplomatic channels open. In a post on X, the Indian High Commission said Trivedi reiterated India's commitment to working with Bangladesh in a "positive, constructive and forward-looking manner".Holding her first public press conference since her ouster exactly two years ago, former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina reiterated her determination to return to her country by the end of this year. Addressing virtually the media gathering in Delhi, Hasina provided her version of events that led her to flee Bangladesh. She asserted that a conspiracy had been hatched to misguide genuine students, who protested against her govt, leading to its dissolution.Highlighting the violent character of the 2024 upheaval, Hasina said that hundreds of offices belonging to her Awami League party were vandalised, houses of Awami leaders were burnt, policemen attacked and killed, and thousands of Awami supporters were assaulted and murdered. Yet, the Muhammad Yunus-led interim govt passed an indemnity ordinance, later converted into a law, to protect the violent protesters.“I, myself, had instituted a judicial inquiry commission to investigate all the cases of violence independently, so that the truth could be known. But after the Yunus regime seized power, they stopped the work of the commission. If they had nothing to hide, why would they prevent the inquiry?” said Hasina. Alleging continuing violence and persecution under the current BNP-led govt, Hasina said that at least 10,000 Awami leaders and workers have been killed or disappeared. “Many Awami leaders, intellectuals and workers also continue to languish in jail without due process or trial, and they have been subjected to torture and denial of their legal rights.”Hasina’s son and senior Awami leader, Sajeeb Wazed Joy, who also joined the press conference virtually from the US, stressed on the indemnity point. “None of the police killings, per the indemnity law, can be prosecuted. So, my question is this: Are killings acceptable? If you can have blanket immunity for protesters who killed police officers, killed civilians and Awami League members and leaders, then why blame anybody?”
Article Summary: Bangladesh pm tariq rehman has called for a "conducive environment" to improve ties with india. His comments come as dhaka continues to seek new delhi's cooperation on the extradition of ousted prime minister sheikh hasina. Hasina has been living in india since the fall of her government and was sentenced to death in november.

Article Title: "Erika prefers to grieve with Charlie’s enemies": Candace Owens takes aim at Erika Kirk again as Charlie Kirk feud erupts over controversial reporter
Article Text:
Candace Owens targets Erika Kirk over Brandy Zadrozny interview

Why Candace Owens says Erika Kirk’s decision raised questions

Candace Owens has reignited her public dispute with Erika Kirk, this time accusing Charlie Kirk ’s widow of working with people Owens says were hostile toward the late conservative activist. Her latest comments focus on journalist Brandy Zadrozny and an interview with Erika, adding another tense chapter to a feud that has already drawn intense attention across conservative media.Owens’ latest criticism centers on Erika Kirk’s decision to speak with Brandy Zadrozny, a journalist who has written critically about Charlie Kirk and his political legacy.Owens argued that Charlie strongly disliked Zadrozny and questioned why Erika would agree to an interview with her after his death.“Charlie Kirk hated this reporter Brandy. So much so that when she contacted me almost immediately after his assassination, I had a visceral reaction—told her to kick rocks, and reminded her how nasty she had been to Charlie and TPUSA. It is of course, expected that Charlie’s wife didn’t care about that at all and chose to open the doors up, and grant Brandy an interview— despite the nasty articles that Brandy wrote about Charlie which are STILL available on the internet.Owens continued with an even stronger accusation:“I have learned that Erika prefers to grieve with Charlie’s enemies. I’m glad Brandy included my response to her in this trash piece.”The comments reflect the wider conflict between Owens and Erika, which has continued for months. Owens has repeatedly questioned aspects of Charlie Kirk’s death and Erika’s leadership of Turning Point USA. Her claims have been disputed, and there is no established evidence that Erika was involved in her husband’s death.Owens also reposted a statement Zadrozny had made after Charlie’s death. The journalist wrote:“Charlie Kirk trafficked in conspiracy theories. In death, he became the main character in the ultimate one, spun by the White House. It’s a tactic I imagined Kirk would have approved of.”Owens reacted strongly, writing:“Can you imagine sitting down with the woman who authored this tweet, just six days after tour husband was murdered? Insulting your husband as a conspiracy theorist? I’m sorry but I just cannot with any person still pretending there isn’t something deeply wrong with Erika Kirk immediately taking over her husband’s organization, only to partner and collude with all of his enemies.”She added:“Please just stop pretending any of this is normal. It feels like we are in the throes of the longest running Dateline episode ever.”The remarks have intensified an already bitter public disagreement. Owens’ broader campaign against Erika has previously included her “Bride of Charlie” series, which examined Erika’s personal life and leadership of TPUSA. Independent reporting has noted that several of Owens’ allegations surrounding Erika have lacked supporting evidence.The dispute has become larger than one interview. It now reflects a deeper split over how Charlie Kirk’s legacy, death and political organization should be discussed publicly.Owens continues to raise questions, while Erika has taken on leadership of TPUSA and has faced intense scrutiny since her husband’s death.For now, the most explosive claims remain allegations rather than established facts. That distinction matters, particularly when discussion involves an active criminal case and accusations against living people.
Article Summary: Candace owens accuses erika kirk of working with people hostile to the late conservative activist. Her latest comments focus on journalist brandy zadrozny and an interview with erika. Owens has repeatedly questioned aspects of charlie kirk’s death and erika's leadership of turning point usa.

Article Title: Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express (which has only single aisles) and then move to AI (which has wide body aircraft too that have higher pay) for a “strong foundation for progression within the group”. The group has tried to do multiple things — make AI Express more attractive for pilots through better pay and address shortage there mainly on the Boeing 737 fleet; check resignations and retain cockpit crew.AI pilots have for years been facing a 40 hour guaranteed pay — meaning they will get minimum for these many hours irrespective of actual flying and flying more will for more pay — while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. This has been a cause of heartburn among pilots. Under the revised framework while AI will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Flying allowance rates beyond 40 hours have also been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Now AI is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb level by next month.The constraint of Pakistan airspace closure remains for Indian carriers and the longer routes they have to take for flying to and from the west — unlike direct routes taken by foreign carriers — means higher flying time and greater pilot requirement.Now a senior commander flying for about 55 hours in a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh at present. And a first officer doing so will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh as of now.While privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24, the airline will not be counting mandatory weekly off time pilots get as per regulatory requirement and the new leave structure accounts does not factor that which comes across as a cut in leave, said people in the know. IndiGo may relook at its leave policy too for pilots.Since Tata Group took over AI and AI Express in Jan 2022, the Maharaja has lost over Rs 55,000 crore due to multiple factors. The pilot pay hike announced Friday indicates it is looking at the future and preparing for growth with hundreds of aircraft on order without being bogged down by the tumultuous recent past.“New career pathways, enhanced compensation and benefits, and improved quality-of-life initiatives support Air India Group's next phase of expansion. At the heart of these initiatives is a clear, structured and transparent career pathway that provides faster command opportunities, long-term progression and access to one of the most significant widebody growth programmes in global aviation,” said an official.Since 2022, AI Group has grown from around 100 aircraft to nearly 300 aircraft and has placed orders for 600 new aircraft, including 80 wide body aircraft. Tatas are investing in capability building, including the establishment of a modern aviation academy in Gurugram with Airbus and Boeing full-flight simulators, and a new flying training school in Amravati, Maharashtra.“As AI group expands, it is focused on developing and retaining internal talent through a structured progression model across Air India Express and Air India. Pilots across Air India and Air India Express will operate under a common seniority framework, creating an integrated and transparent pathway for career progression across the group. This framework provides greater visibility into future opportunities while ensuring a consistent and structured approach to advancement,” said teh official.Under the new framework, AI Express will serve as “the primary pathway for pilots seeking command upgrades. This approach is designed to accelerate command opportunities, enable pilots to build command experience earlier in their careers, and create a strong foundation for progression within the Group.”Following command experience at AI Express, pilots will have the opportunity to progress to Air India and subsequently pursue widebody flying and command opportunities. “With 80 additional widebody aircraft on order and scheduled for induction over the coming years, Air India offers pilots a long-term pathway that is unique in the Indian market,” the official said. An additional incentive is being offered to pilots who sign up to support the growing Boeing 737 fleet in Air India Express under which they will receive a fleet allowance.
Article Summary: Commanders get the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. First officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in ai express. They will then move to ai (which has wide body aircraft too that have higher pay) an additional incentive is being offered to pilots who sign up to support the growing boeing 737 fleet in air india express.

Article Title: Italy’s Andrea Doria sank in 1956, but divers still explore its dangerous wreck despite 18 deaths
Article Text:
Representative Image of the Andrea Doria liner partially submerged amid fog and ocean currents (AI-generated image)

How the Andrea Doria sank after colliding with the Stockholm in 1956

Why divers call it the Mount Everest of wreck diving

How mixed gas diving changed what was possible at the wreck

What divers recovered from the wreck in 2025

Why salvage from the wreck remains a contested question

Seventy years after the Andrea Doria sank in the North Atlantic, divers are still descending to the deteriorating Italian liner, exploring newly exposed sections and recovering artefacts before parts of the wreck disappear for good. Eighteen divers have died while trying to explore it. The ship lies on its starboard side about 50 miles south of Nantucket, with the seabed roughly 250 feet below the surface, well beyond normal recreational diving depths. Powerful currents, limited visibility, cold water and long decompression stops make the descent demanding, while collapsing passages, loose metal and heavy silt add to the danger inside the ship itself. Decades on the seafloor have already reshaped the wreck, with whole decks collapsed and the vessel now standing about 30 feet shorter than it once did.The Andrea Doria left Genoa on July 17, 1956, carrying 1,706 passengers and crew, bound for New York on what would become its 101st and final transatlantic crossing. On July 25, nearing the end of that voyage, the ship ran into dense fog while the outbound liner Stockholm sailed in clearer conditions nearby, and officers on both vessels reached different conclusions about how to pass each other after tracking one another by radar.At 11.05 pm, the Andrea Doria's captain ordered a four-degree turn to port, and two minutes later the Stockholm's third officer ordered a roughly 22-degree turn to starboard. By the time the two ships spotted each other's lights at 11.10 pm, less than a mile separated them, and neither manoeuvre could prevent what followed. Less than a minute later, the Stockholm's reinforced bow struck the Andrea Doria's starboard side at 18.5 knots, driving about 40 feet into the larger ship and tearing open seven of its 11 decks just behind the bridge. The collision killed 46 people aboard the Andrea Doria and five aboard the Stockholm, though the liner stayed afloat for nearly 11 hours, long enough for nearby ships to rescue the remaining passengers before it finally sank the next morning.Divers reached the wreck almost immediately, with two men descending to it the very next day using wetsuits, basic equipment and an underwater camera, and expeditions have continued ever since. The site earned its nickname among divers because of both the difficulty of the descent and the dangers of entering the wreck itself, and eight divers died there between 1992 and 1999 alone. Rising about 80 feet from the seabed, the ship exposes divers to roughly six to eight times the pressure found at the surface, and they burn through their air supply at a similarly increased rate, raising the risk of narcosis, oxygen toxicity and decompression sickness. Inside the hull, divers must navigate sideways stairways, collapsing passages, decaying metal and dangling wires, and any silt disturbed along the way can billow into the water and sharply cut visibility within seconds.In 1996, divers Steve Gatto and Tom Packer became the first to reach the ship's engine room, and while filming its gauge panel, Gatto lost track of his exit route and began experiencing narcosis before finding his way back out using one of the strobe lights the pair had placed along their path. Mixed gas diving later allowed divers to replace some of the nitrogen in their tanks with helium, reducing narcosis and making deeper dives more manageable, though the technique brought its own complications, since divers still needed lengthy decompression stops and had to carry the correct gas mixture for each depth or risk a fatal mistake. Gatto, who has made more than 250 dives to the Andrea Doria over the years, has said some divers were substituting technology for the experience needed to dive safely.On July 11, 2025, diver Chris Ogden was around 230 feet below the surface inside a confined section of the wreck when he spotted the circular top of a gyrocompass repeater, a five-foot-tall brass navigation instrument that once stood on the ship's bridge wing. With only four dives left on the expedition and barely 40 minutes on the bottom each time, Ogden and his diving partner Joe Mazraani spent most of three dives clearing nets, cables and roughly eight feet of debris before finally freeing the instrument and lifting it to the surface using an inflatable bag rated for 500 pounds. The gyrocompass reached the surface largely intact, though its face was missing, and weeks later filmmaker Al Giddings came forward saying he had recovered that same piece decades earlier during a 1968 expedition and still had it in his home.Atlantic Wreck Salvage, whose ongoing recovery work at the site is documented on its own record of the Andrea Doria's history and diving conditions, has made annual trips to the wreck since 2010 and restores what it recovers for public display. Removing artefacts from historic shipwrecks continues to divide opinion, with some arguing that objects should remain in place or be recovered only by trained archaeologists, while divers who work the Andrea Doria counter that its rapid deterioration means items left behind risk being crushed or buried for good as more of the structure collapses. The wreck sits within a stretch of ocean that the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's Stellwagen Bank National Marine Sanctuary recognises as part of the region's protected maritime heritage, underlining how significant these sites remain even as they continue to change. Seven decades after it went down, the Andrea Doria keeps exposing new sections of itself to the divers willing to reach it, even as more of the ship settles permanently into the seabed.
Article Summary: Andrea doria sank after colliding with the stockholm in 1956. Ship lies on its starboard side about 50 miles south of nantucket. Decades on the seafloor have reshaped the wreck, with whole decks collapsed. Eight divers have died while trying to explore it. The gyrocompass reached the surface largely intact, though its face was missing.

Article Title: For India, the Mecca pact is a setback. For China, it's a warning
Article Text:
Mecca pact: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia & Turkey’s defence deal might end up being a big headache for China.

The Mecca agreement aims to strengthen defence cooperation and collective deterrence among Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

What about China

Why China should be wary of it

The Mecca pact may provide the US more leeway to put extra focus on the Indo-Pacific region and China.

The big picture

What's next

Pakistan, Saudi Arabia , and Turkey signed a Nato-style mutual defence agreement in Mecca on August 7, declaring that "any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all”.There is no other way to put it: The new Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Turkey defence pact is a setback for India. True, it’s not directly aimed at India and one of the main financers of the deal, Saudi Arabia, is not agnostic towards India. In fact, India-Saudi Arabia ties have grown many folds in recent years.But, if Pakistan is involved in any defence pact and that too as a net security provider, India will have to take note of it. Kanwal Sibal, India’s former foreign secretary, described the development as a "very negative development for Indian interests".The pact may embolden Pakistan to take a more belligerent attitude towards India. Even if Saudi Arabia refuses to support Pakistan militarily in an India-Pakistan conflict, Islamabad could potentially benefit from intelligence cooperation, weapons flows, diplomatic support or financial assistance.Then, there is the issue of growing defence cooperation between Pakistan and Turkey. It was quite visible during Operation Sindoor. So, the Mecca pact is definitely a concerning development for India.For now, Beijing looks like a quiet winner. Its entire approach to the Gulf has rested on staying friendly with everyone at once. It's been arming Pakistan, buying Iranian oil, courting Saudi Arabia and Turkey, and doing business with the UAE without ever picking a side.With the new defence pact, Chinese weapon systems could even gain greater access to Gulf markets through Pakistan.But that is only half the story.The Mecca pact could also become a strategic setback for China if it succeeds in doing what Washington increasingly wants its partners to do: Assume a larger share of their own defence burden.“The Pak-KSA-Turkey agreement is a logical outgrowth of the deepening security ties of these 3 countries in recent months. With its focus on collective regional deterrence with an eye to Iran, it’ll be received well in Washington, which wants to see more burden-sharing from top allies,” Michael Kugelman of the Atlantic Council wrote on X.A more self-reliant Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan could reduce the need for constant US military attention in West Asia. That, in turn, could give Washington greater capacity to concentrate on its principal long-term competitor: China.The US regards China, not Russia or Iran, as its principal long-term strategic competitor.Any potential reduction in American military burdens in West Asia may allow Washington to devote additional resources on the Indo-Pacific front, critical minerals, advanced technology, supply-chain resilience and alliances surrounding China.That is the paradox at the heart of the Mecca agreement.China could still profit commercially. Pakistani familiarity with Chinese equipment could introduce more Chinese systems into Saudi Arabia. Beijing could remain an important diplomatic and economic partner for every member of the pact.But those gains may incur costs too."China would be careful not to become a major arms supplier to the region to undermine US interests there. US can step up arms supplies to Taiwan in retaliation," Kanwal Sibal wrote on X.For Beijing, the most consequential lesson from the upheaval stretching from Ukraine to the Gulf may not be the emergence of another regional defence alliance. It’s about how difficult modern wars have become to even end on favourable terms.The US and Israel have inflicted enormous damage on Iran, but have yet to force Tehran into submission or eliminate its ability to impose costs across the Gulf. Russia, despite its vastly larger military and economic resources, has also failed to secure a decisive victory over Ukraine after years of war. Both conflicts underline an uncomfortable reality of our times: Military alliance or superiority is no guarantee for a win even against a weaker adversary.That matters enormously for Taiwan. Both Russia-Ukraine and Israel-US-Iran wars may make China wary of going for a forced unification of Taiwan.Chinese President Xi Jinping has made reunification with Taiwan a defining national objective. As per reports, Xi’s plan for the PLA is to have the military capability to go for a unification with Taiwan by 2027. This looks increasingly difficult, though.At the same time, China's increasingly muscular diplomacy and military posture have produced their own counter-reaction in East Asia. Japan is accelerating its military build-up, expanding strike capabilities and treating a Taiwan contingency as increasingly relevant to its own security. What Beijing once dismissed as the fading architecture of US power in Asia is, in several respects, becoming more militarised in response to China's rise.That is the paradox of China's “wolf warrior” era: Pressure intended to make neighbouring countries accommodate Beijing has also encouraged some of them to strengthen military cooperation with Washington and spend more on defence.The crucial question is whether the Mecca pact remains political deterrence or develops into genuine military integration. Joint exercises will matter. So will intelligence-sharing, command structures, defence-industrial partnerships, technology transfers and procurement decisions.For India, the key test will be whether Saudi Arabia allows Pakistan to internationalise future India-Pakistan confrontations through the new framework.For China, watch something different: Whether the pact actually provides the US more leeway to put extra focus on the Indo-Pacific region.
Article Summary: Mecca pact: pakistan, saudi arabia & turkey’s defence deal might end up being a big headache for china. The mecca agreement aims to strengthen defence cooperation and collective deterrence among turkey. Saudi arabia and pakistan. Both russia-ukraine and israel-us-iran wars may make china wary of going for a forced unification of taiwan.

Article Title: Balen ends 'envoy snub' with India-first reset; meets China envoy within hours
Article Text:
Indian envoy Naveen Srivastava and Nepal PM Balen Shah discuss 'bilateral cooperation and development partnership'

NEW DELHI: Nepal PM Balendra Shah on Monday ended his self-imposed bar on one-on-one meetings with Kathmandu-based foreign envoys, receiving Indian ambassador Naveen Srivastava first and Chinese ambassador Zhang Maoming hours later at Singha Durbar in a diplomatic reset after months of a distancing that had increasingly come into question in Kathmandu and beyond. Shah is scheduled to meet US Embassy chargé d’affaires Scott Urbom on Tuesday extending the outreach beyond Nepal’s two neighbours.Shah and Srivastava discussed bilateral ties, mutual interests, development partnership and cooperation, with Shah stressing the need to deepen Nepal’s “historic relationship” with India. PMO said on social media that the talks focused on “further strengthening Nepal-India relations”, bilateral cooperation and development partnership.Srivastava said on X that he conveyed “warm greetings from Prime Minister Modi ji” and described the meeting as an “engaging & productive exchange” to deepen the “robust, multi-faceted India-Nepal partnership”. Neither side disclosed whether specific issues such as the boundary dispute, power trade or Shah’s proposed India visit figured in the talks.The India-first sequencing was significant. A senior foreign ministry official had told a Kathmandu-based daily before the meetings, “The Indian ambassador is told to come first, followed by the Chinese ambassador,” adding that the timing reflected govt’s foreign-policy priority.The two meetings had initially been planned about two weeks ago but were deferred after communal violence in Sunsari and other districts.Monday’s exchanges also contrasted with friction during Shah’s first weeks in office. His administration strictly enforced customs duties on low-value goods brought from India and protested to both New Delhi and Beijing over resumption of the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage through Lipulekh, which Nepal claims. Shah also refused to meet Indian foreign secretary Vikram Misri on protocol grounds. Misri’s planned May 11-12 Kathmandu visit was subsequently postponed.The reset came with Shah’s first India visit as PM still pending. Modi invited him soon after the latter took office on March 27 and Shah accepted, but no date has been fixed. India formally reiterated on July 28 that the invitation remained open.RSP president Rabi Lamichhane had received unusually high-profile treatment during his five-day India visit in June. BJP welcomed Lamichhane with a floral shower at its headquarters, where party president Nitin Nabin received him, before he met PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and NSA Ajit Doval. The reception drew attention because Shah’s govt had described Lamichhane’s trip as “a purely personal trip”.The stakes for the Himalayan nation extend beyond protocol: India accounts for over 60% of Nepal’s trade and almost all its third-country transit, while Shah’s govt has simultaneously sought greater Chinese investment, technology and tourism. Foreign minister Shisir Khanal has described India as a major potential market for Nepal’s electricity and China as an important source of tourists.
Article Summary: Nepal pm balendra shah ends his self-imposed bar on one-on-one meetings with foreign envoys. He received indian ambassador naveen srivastava first and chinese ambassador zhang maoming hours later at singha durbar. Shah is scheduled to meet us embassy chargé d’affaires scott urbom on tuesday.

Article Title: Buildings collapse, panic grips residents as quake shakes Colombia - 10 visuals that capture horror
Article Text:
A 7.4-magnitude earthquake rocked western Colombia causing widespread damage

A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, killing at least 77 people and causing widespread destruction across several cities, news agency Reuters reported.Buildings collapsed, residents rushed out of homes and panic spread as strong tremors were felt as far away as Bogotá and neighbouring Ecuador.The epicentre was near San José del Palmar in the Chocó region, around 400 km west of Bogotá, at a depth of about 107 km, according to the US geological survey.The earthquake caused significant damage at Matecaña International Airport in Pereira, where strong tremors sent people into a panic.The Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary in Manizales suffered major damage, with a large crack appearing along its facade. One of its towers also collapsed onto the nave.The earthquake struck with enough force to shake Pereira airport, where people were seen reacting to the sudden tremors.Several buildings collapsed in Cali, with footage showing the extent of the destruction caused by the quake.In Pereira, several buildings collapsed and people were reportedly trapped inside the rubble.Manizales reported several deaths, while the city also witnessed damage to its historic neo-Gothic cathedral.In Quibdó, Chocó Governor Nubia Córdoba reported injuries and serious damage to buildings, with homes and other structures affected by the earthquake.The powerful tremors triggered panic and evacuations in Bogotá, hundreds of kilometres from the epicentre, as residents rushed out of buildings.Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella said he would personally supervise recovery operations and establish an emergency centre in San José del Palmar.The earthquake was also felt in neighbouring Ecuador, as authorities continued to assess damage and casualties.
Article Summary: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western colombia on monday, killing at least 77 people and causing widespread destruction. The epicentre was near san josé del palmar in the chocó region, around 400 km west of bogotá, at a depth of about 107 km. Buildings collapsed, residents rushed out of homes and panic spread as strong tremors were felt.

Article Title: Indian expat from Kerala killed in Dubai gas cylinder blast; colleague recalls moments before explosion
Article Text:
Shijin Paul/Image: X

Colleague recounts fire before blast

Explosion struck during firefighting efforts

An Indian-origin man from Kerala was killed in a gas cylinder explosion at a car showroom on Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai on Monday, the Indian Consulate in Dubai confirmed, Gulf News reported.The victim was identified as Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district.A relative told the outlet that Shijin succumbed to his injuries at a hospital after the explosion."I was informed by his company about the blast. Unfortunately, he had passed away by the time I reached the hospital," the relative said.Shijin worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. According to his family, he had joined the company in November. He is survived by his parents and wife.A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises."Some of us, including Shijin and I, went out of our showroom after some of our colleagues alerted us about a fire," Abid, a photographer who worked with Shijin, told the newspaper."There were people from several shops nearby too, not just from our showroom.Many people came running after spotting the fire."Abid said the flames appeared to have broken out near a gate close to neighbouring auto service workshops."There is a gate in one corner of the showroom, and the fire started somewhere there. There are some auto service companies next to our showroom, and the fire was near their location."According to Abid, people at the scene attempted to contain the fire with extinguishers before the cylinder exploded."People were trying to put out the fire with fire extinguishers. The explosion occurred while efforts were underway to douse the fire. Everyone ran away," he said.He added that he did not immediately realise Shijin had been caught in the blast."I don't know who all got hit. I got to know about his death later," Abid said.The Indian Consulate said it remains in contact with Shijin's family and the authorities to provide support following the incident.
Article Summary: Victim identified as shijin paul, 27, from kottarakkara in kerala's kollam district. A relative said that he succumbed to his injuries at a hospital after the explosion. A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire.
